newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ANGELS MOVE BACK INTO FIRST BY BEATING BREWERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ANGELS MOVE BACK INTO FIRST BY BEATING BREWERS.

text.p: Dennis Springer tossed a
six-hitter and Todd Greene smacked a three-run homer as the
Anaheim Angels moved into a first-place tie in the American
League West by beating the Milwaukee Brewers 5-1 Thursday.
Springer (8-5) struck out one and did not walk a batter in
recording his fifth career complete game and third this
season, helping the Angels moved back into a tie with the idle
Seattle Mariners. He beat Milwaukee for the second time this
season as the Angels halted their three-game losing streak.
"We needed the win to get back going again," Angels
manager Terry Collins said. "Dennis Springer did exactly what
you hoped he would -- that is, come in here and pitch like he
can."
Third baseman Jeff Cirillo's bobble of Tim Salmon's
grounder opened the gates for a four-run fourth inning.
"I hate making errors, especially in a situation like
that, when they turn around and score four runs off you,"
Cirillo said. "I take it personally."
"We are own worst enemy in these games now," Milwaukee
manager Phil Garner said.
Jack Howell also homered in the ninth for Anaheim.
Jose Mercedes (4-7) gave up five runs and eight hits over
eight innings. He is 1-5 in his last 10 starts.
The Brewers dropped their third game in a row at County
Stadium.
Outfielder Rickey Henderson, acquired by the Angels from
from the Padres the day before, played left field and batted
leadoff, going 0-5 with one strikeout.
"It's not bad being back here (American League),"
Henderson said. "I know what it's all about. The biggest thing
is just getting adjusted to the team and seeing what they need
and what I can do to help win the division. It's always nice
coming to a contender."
In New York, recently activated Tim Raines doubled home a
pair of runs and Tino Martinez followed with a two-run single
as the Yankees rallied for five runs in the seventh to defeat
the Kansas City Royals 10-5.
Raines, activated before Tuesday's series opener, added an
RBI double in the fifth and scored twice. Martinez, the
American League leader in RBI, added run-scoring singles in
the first and eighth to push his RBI total to 113.
The win moved the Yankees within four games of the
first-place Orioles in the American League East.
David Wells (14-5) allowed four runs and nine hits in 7
1/3 innings in winning his fourth straight start.
Gregg Olson (1-1) was tagged for all five runs in the
seventh. The Yankees added three more runs in the eighth
against reliever Mike Perez.
Chili Davis hit a pair of solo homers for the Royals, who
have dropped seven of their last 10.
In Baltimore, the game between the Seattle Mariners and
the Orioles was postponed due to an electrical failure at
Camden Yards and has been rescheduled as part of a day-night
doubleheader on Friday.
When the lights were turned on at Camden Yards, several
banks did not illuminate, leaving parts of the field dark.
In Cleveland, Charles Nagy threw eight strong innings at
the Detroit Tigers and David Justice led a 15-hit attack with
a three-run homer and four RBI, powering the Indians to a 12-1
rout.
Nagy (12-8) gave up one run and did not allow a hit over
his last five innings. He is 3-1 against the Tigers with a
1.41 ERA this season and 13-4 lifetime against them.
Manny Ramirez had three hits, including a solo homer,
three runs and two RBI, and Jim Thome added a two-run homer
and drove in three runs for the Indians, who are batting .356
and averaging 7.4 runs per game over their last five contests.
Cleveland has won four of six games and extended its lead
to 3 1/2 games over the White Sox in the A.L. Central.
In Chicago, Jason Giambi, Matt Stairs and Ernie Young each
homered and drove in three runs as the Oakland Athletics had
their best offensive output of the season in a 12-5 victory
over the White Sox.
Giambi and Brent Mayne each had three of Oakland's 15 hits
as the Athletics won for the sixth time in eight games.
In Boston, Nomar Garciaparra's run-scoring single snapped
a tie and sparked a five-run eighth inning as the Red Sox beat
Brad Radke for the third time this season and snapped a
three-game losing streak, 6-1 over the Minnesota Twins.
Radke (16-7) had retired 13 straight batters before the
dam burst in the eighth.
Garciaparra had his 51st multi-hit game, tops in the
American League. The rookie has hit in 17 straight games.
Radke was reached for six runs and seven hits with five
strikeouts in seven-plus innings. He has lost all three of his
starts to Boston this season.
Jeff Suppan (6-1) allowed one run and six hits with two
walks and five strikeouts in a career-high eight innings.
